Chapter 9: Problem-Solving Together—Generating Options and Building Agreements.
Once you’ve built real understanding and set aside the blame game, you’re ready to shift into solution mode. Now it’s about rolling up your sleeves and working together to find answers that actually work for both sides.
So, how do you do that? Joint problem-solving usually takes a few key steps—let’s walk through them together.
First, focus on interests, not just positions. Instead of getting stuck on, “I need it my way,” try asking, “What’s really important to you about this?” Digging into those underlying needs makes it easier to find common ground.
Next, open the floor for brainstorming. Let creativity flow! Say, “Let’s throw out every idea we can think of—even the wild ones.” You never know which option will spark a real solution.
Then, look at your list together and weigh the pros and cons. Which options meet the most needs on both sides? Sometimes the best answer is a mix of ideas, rather than picking just one.
After that, make sure you actually build a clear agreement. Summarize what you’ve decided, spell out the next steps, and double-check that everyone’s on the same page. For example, you might say, “So we’ll try this plan for a month, then check in to see how it’s working.”
Want to see how this looks in real life? Imagine two roommates at odds over cleaning. One just wants a tidy space to relax, while the other gets overwhelmed by strict schedules. Once they talk about what really matters to each of them, they can brainstorm—maybe they’ll alternate cleaning weeks or even chip in for a cleaning service now and then. Suddenly, they’ve come up with something that works for both.
Think of joint problem-solving as building a bridge. Each person brings their own materials, and together, you create something stronger than either could on their own. Sure, there might be bumps along the way, and sometimes compromise is part of the process. But when everyone feels heard and involved, those solutions are much more likely to last.
And here’s something to remember—agreements shouldn’t be set in stone. Life changes, right? So make it a habit to check in once in a while. Revisiting what you’ve agreed on helps keep trust strong and the conversation open.
